main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can use the small room for 15-minute daily practice without clashing with A's client calls, B's file access, and C's private call

A-B.evidence: A and B each raised separate objections (turns 1, 4). A later said the files are for D and B to work out (22), and B's file fix (23) removes her objection, but A and B never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: A and C raised separate time conflicts (turns 1, 12). Both ended up accepting D's adjusted times (8, 19, 20), but they never spoke to each other.

A-D.evidence: A rejected the 4:30 time and the sign (1, 3, 6). D offered other times and asked for ideas (2, 7). A proposed 3:45 (8) and D accepted it (21). A also offered 'is 3.45 okay' (20).

B-C.evidence: B's file worry (4, 9, 11) and C's call timing (12, 14) are separate points. Both end up accepting the arrangement, but they never interact.

B-D.evidence: B said any time was a problem (9, 11). D asked how often she needed files (10), then asked how it would work (21). B proposed archiving files (23), D agreed and offered to help (25), and they set a time (26-27).

C-D.evidence: C said 1 p.m. was a problem (12). D offered 12:45 or 1:15 and flexibility (18). C replied 'that works for me' (19).
